chunks: And Shaykh Abu ʿAbd Allah informed me, from Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Hamzah al-ʿAlawi, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from ʿAbbad ibn Sulayman, from Saʿd ibn Saʿd, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, concerning:

A well such that between it and the privy there are five cubits, or less, or more—can wudu (ablution) be performed from it? He عليه السلام said: It is not disliked, whether from nearness or distance; wudu (ablution) may be performed from it and ghusl (ritual bath) may be done, so long as the water has not changed.
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report indicates that all the previous reports are to be understood as referring to recommendation, not prohibition and obligation.

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well from which water is drawn
key_terms.الْكَنِيفِ: the privy or lavatory near the well
key_terms.خَمْسَةُ أَذْرُعٍ: a distance of five cubits mentioned in the ruling

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use water from a well near a privy for wudu (ablution) and ghusl (ritual bath)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on using water from a well located near a privy. It states that wudu (ablution) and ghusl (ritual bath) are permissible from such a well regardless of proximity, so long as the water has not undergone change, and al-Shaykh interprets earlier reports on distance as indicating recommendation rather than strict obligation or prohibition.
